content: If you are currently taking sulfisoxazole, it is important to contact your doctor to discuss transitioning to an alternative treatment. Sulfisoxazole, a sulfa-based antibiotic, is used to eliminate bacteria responsible for infections, particularly those affecting the urinary tract and ears. However, antibiotics like sulfisoxazole are ineffective against colds, flu, or other viral infections. This medication may also be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Sulfisoxazole is available in tablet and liquid forms for oral administration. It is typically taken four times daily for a duration of 10 to 14 days or longer, as directed by your doctor. Each dose should be consumed with a full glass of water. If using the liquid form, shake the bottle well before each dose to ensure the medication is evenly mixed. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take sulfisoxazole exactly as prescribed, without altering the dosage or frequency. Before starting sulfisoxazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to sulfisoxazole, other sulfa drugs, diuretics (commonly known as water pills), oral diabetes medications, or any other drugs. Additionally, provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), cyclosporine, diabetes medications, methotrexate, phenytoin, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of liver or kidney disease, asthma, severe allergies, or glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G-6-PD) deficiency, an inherited blood disorder. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Should you become pregnant while taking sulfisoxazole, contact your doctor immediately. Avoid unnecessary or prolonged exposure to sunlight, and use protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen, as sulfisoxazole may increase your skin's sensitivity to sunlight. Sulfisoxazole may cause stomach upset. To minimize this, take the medication with food or milk. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Sulfisoxazole may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following mild side effects, especially if they persist or worsen: Diarrhea Dizziness or loss of balance Loss of appetite Upset stomach If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: Skin rash or changes in skin appearance Sore throat Fever Headache Joint or muscle pain Yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice) Swelling of the lips or tongue Difficulty swallowing Fatigue Unusual bleeding or bruising Weakness If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store sulfisoxazole in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on safe disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as your doctor will order specific tests to monitor your response to sulfisoxazole. Do not share this medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If your symptoms persist after completing the course of sulfisoxazole, contact your doctor.
